note: Bridger-Teton NF (Big Piney Ranger District) campground on Middle Piney Creek just east of Middle Piney Lake, about 24 miles west of Big Piney via WY-350, the Middle Piney Road and forest roads. Shaded sites among trees; pack it in, pack it out. Host typically July 1 to Labor Day. Straight Creek Trailhead is just east. --Claude
summary: FS page + layout sign read: 24 sites, FCFS only, $10, vault toilets, hydrant spring water, no hookups, Memorial Day-Labor Day. FS: 'sites large enough to accommodate smaller trailers (not large ones)' - criteria flag (no 23-ft+ review found). Stored '~40 ft' and '2WD-passable' dropped from the note (unsourced; the first contradicted). Phone empty -> 307-276-5800. Pin fine.
flags: FIT (criteria, report): the FS singles this campground out: 'there are sites large enough to accommodate smaller trailers (not large ones)'. No length is posted; the layout sign gives none. inclusion_evidence's 'vehicles to 40 ft' and the note's 'vehicles to ~40 ft' have no source on the current pages and are contradicted by this wording - dropped. Whether this is Bridger-Teton boilerplate was not established (two sister-page slugs tried answered 'Page not found'). A web search found no dated review in which the reviewer's own 23-ft+ rig fit (a Hipcamp reviewer: it 'probably can't fit a ton of big rigs'; large trailers use free dispersed spots before the campground turnoff). Under the 2026-11-02 rule (unclear fit = keep with a caveat) the sites note carries the FS wording.
PHONE: empty -> 307-276-5800 (Big Piney Ranger District, on the FS page and the layout sign). Website confirmed. No recreation.gov listing (first-come).
NOTE: '2WD-passable' (unsourced; the FS says nothing about the road) and 'bear bins' (not on the FS page or sign) dropped along with the structured repeats.

PIN: stored 42.61723,-110.53280 sits in the north part of the loop (FS point 42.61847,-110.53108 is ~200 m NE on the access road) - no move. WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept; the FS says the campground is 'located on Middle Piney Creek', but the loop is under canopy and the creek's position relative to the sites can't be read on imagery - a creekside lead only if a later source names creek sites.
